revisions.name: Barbarian
revisions.summary: Hit Dice: 1d12 per barbarian level. Hit Points at 1st Level: 12 + your Constitution modifier. Hit Points at Higher Levels: 1d12 (or 7) + your Constitution modifier per barbarian level after 1st. Armor: Light armor, medium armor, shields. Weapons: Simple weapons, martial weapons. Tools: None. Saving Throws: Strength, Constitution. Skills: Choose two from Animal Handling, Athletics, Intimidation, Nature, Perception, and Survival. TomeStack: levels 1-20.

effects.text: Skills: Choose two from Animal Handling, Athletics, Intimidation, Nature, Perception, and Survival.
Primal Path. At 3rd level, you choose a path that shapes the nature of your rage. (The SRD 5.1 includes the Path of the Berserker.)
Multiclassing prerequisite: Strength 13. Multiclassing proficiencies gained: shields, simple weapons, martial weapons (SRD 5.1 pp. 56-57).

revisions.name: Rage
revisions.summary:
In battle, you fight with primal ferocity. On your turn, you can enter a rage as a bonus action.

While raging, you gain the following benefits if you aren’t wearing heavy armor:
• You have advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws.
• When you make a melee weapon attack using Strength, you gain a bonus to the damage roll that increases as you gain levels as a barbarian, as shown in the Rage Damage column of the Barbarian table.
• You have resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage.

If you are able to cast spells, you can’t cast them or concentrate on them while raging.

Your rage lasts for 1 minute. It ends early if you are knocked unconscious or if your turn ends and you haven’t attacked a hostile creature since your last turn or taken damage since then. You can also end your rage on your turn as a bonus action.

Once you have raged the number of times shown for your barbarian level in the Rages column of the Barbarian table, you must finish a long rest before you can rage again.

TomeStack: turning Rage on spends a use (none at 20th level, where the Rages column reads Unlimited) and applies the Rage Damage bonus to your melee attacks, resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage, and advantage on Strength checks and saving throws. Heavy armor, the spell and concentration restrictions, and the early-end conditions are not checked, and the rage is not ended after 1 minute for you: turn Rage off yourself. The damage bonus is added to melee attacks whichever ability they use: a finesse weapon used with Dexterity gets it although the rule says Strength, and a thrown weapon used with Strength does not get it here. Adjust those by hand.

effects.label: Rages
effects.text: The number of times you can rage is the Rages column of the Barbarian table: 2 at levels 1-2, 3 at levels 3-5, 4 at levels 6-11, 5 at levels 12-16 and 6 at levels 17-19. At 20th level the column reads Unlimited: entering the Rage spends nothing.

effects.label: Rage
effects.text: Entering the Rage spends one use (none at 20th level, where the Rages are Unlimited). It lasts 1 minute (10 rounds); the conditions that end it early are by hand.
Rage Damage: the bonus from the Rage Damage column, added to melee attacks while the rage is on.

revisions.name: Unarmored Defense
revisions.summary: While you are not wearing any armor, your Armor Class equals 10 + your Dexterity modifier + your Constitution modifier. You can use a shield and still gain this benefit.

effects.text: Applies only while no armor is worn (the Armor Class breakdown shows it as not used otherwise); a shield is allowed.

revisions.name: Danger Sense
revisions.summary:
At 2nd level, you gain an uncanny sense of when things nearby aren’t as they should be, giving you an edge when you dodge away from danger.

You have advantage on Dexterity saving throws against effects that you can see, such as traps and spells. To gain this benefit, you can’t be blinded, deafened, or incapacitated.

TomeStack: the advantage on Dexterity saving throws is offered as assisted: use it only against effects you can see, and not while you are blinded, deafened, or incapacitated.

effects.text: Only against effects you can see, and not while blinded, deafened, or incapacitated (by hand).

revisions.name: Ability Score Improvement
revisions.summary: When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can’t increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

revisions.name: Extra Attack
revisions.summary: Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

revisions.name: Fast Movement
revisions.summary:
Starting at 5th level, your speed increases by 10 feet while you aren’t wearing heavy armor.

TomeStack: the 10 feet are always added to your speed; take them off by hand while you wear heavy armor.

effects.text: Not while you wear heavy armor (by hand).

revisions.name: Feral Instinct
revisions.summary:
By 7th level, your instincts are so honed that you have advantage on initiative rolls.

Additionally, if you are surprised at the beginning of combat and aren’t incapacitated, you can act normally on your first turn, but only if you enter your rage before doing anything else on that turn.

revisions.name: Brutal Critical
revisions.summary:
Beginning at 9th level, you can roll one additional weapon damage die when determining the extra damage for a critical hit with a melee attack.

This increases to two additional dice at 13th level and three additional dice at 17th level.

revisions.name: Relentless Rage
revisions.summary:
Starting at 11th level, your rage can keep you fighting despite grievous wounds. If you drop to 0 hit points while you’re raging and don’t die outright, you can make a DC 10 Constitution saving throw. If you succeed, you drop to 1 hit point instead.

Each time you use this feature after the first, the DC increases by 5. When you finish a short or long rest, the DC resets to 10.

TomeStack: the damage prompt offers this while your rage is on and sets your hit points to 1; the Constitution saving throw (DC 10, +5 for each use after the first, reset on a short or long rest) is made and tracked by hand.

effects.label: Relentless Rage
effects.text: Make the DC 10 Constitution saving throw first (DC +5 for each use after the first; resets on a short or long rest). On a success you drop to 1 hit point instead.

revisions.name: Persistent Rage
revisions.summary: Beginning at 15th level, your rage is so fierce that it ends early only if you fall unconscious or if you choose to end it.

revisions.name: Indomitable Might
revisions.summary: Beginning at 18th level, if your total for a Strength check is less than your Strength score, you can use that score in place of the total.

revisions.name: Primal Champion
revisions.summary:
At 20th level, you embody the power of the wilds. Your Strength and Constitution scores increase by 4. Your maximum for those scores is now 24.

TomeStack: this increase is not applied to the scores. Add 4 to your Strength and Constitution scores yourself (to a maximum of 24); the sheet then marks every value that reads them as assisted.

effects.text: Strength increases by 4, to a maximum of 24. Not applied: enter the new score by hand.
Constitution increases by 4, to a maximum of 24. Not applied: enter the new score by hand.

revisions.name: Path of the Berserker
revisions.summary: For some barbarians, rage is a means to an end—that end being violence. The Path of the Berserker is a path of untrammeled fury, slick with blood. As you enter the berserker’s rage, you thrill in the chaos of battle, heedless of your own health or well-being.

revisions.name: Mindless Rage
revisions.summary: Beginning at 6th level, you can’t be charmed or frightened while raging. If you are charmed or frightened when you enter your rage, the effect is suspended for the duration of the rage.

revisions.name: Intimidating Presence
revisions.summary:
Beginning at 10th level, you can use your action to frighten someone with your menacing presence. When you do so, choose one creature that you can see within 30 feet of you. If the creature can see or hear you, it must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (DC equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier) or be frightened of you until the end of your next turn. On subsequent turns, you can use your action to extend the duration of this effect on the frightened creature until the end of your next turn. This effect ends if the creature ends its turn out of line of sight or more than 60 feet away from you.

If the creature succeeds on its saving throw, you can’t use this feature on that creature again for 24 hours.

revisions.name: Retaliation
revisions.summary: Starting at 14th level, when you take damage from a creature that is within 5 feet of you, you can use your reaction to make a melee weapon attack against that creature.
